name: slide-marquee-link
title: Slide Marquee Link
author: HoverUI (https://hoverui.com)
description: The label slides up and out while its duplicate arrives from below, reading as one continuous strip moving past a window. It is one strip, not two animated spans: the movement is -50% of the strip's own height, so half of it IS one copy at any type size, with no measurement to drift and no second value to keep in step. Nothing ships to the client: it is a server component with no hooks and no handlers, and the whole effect is CSS. The string is rendered four times — one hidden copy in flow to size the window to exactly one line, two in the moving strip, and an sr-only copy that is the accessible name and the only selectable one, so a drag never copies the word more than once. It reads the hover and :focus-visible of an ancestor `a`, `button`, `[role=button]` or `summary` as well as its own; any other wrapper gets neither. IMPORTANT for keyboard users: the arrived state is pixel-identical to rest — same word, same position — and reduced motion pins the slide off, so the movement is never a focus indicator. If you make this component itself focusable it draws its own outline, which sits on the host outside the clip; if you wrap it in your own link or button, that control must show the focus state and this component will not draw or suppress one for you. Reduced motion holds the strip still — both copies read the same word, so there is no information under the movement to preserve. On touch and any device without hover it rests showing the label. Note: the window is inline-block and clips, so it will not wrap across lines.
